payload.author: funkydude
payload.body:
> In Russian grammar, when writing a date like January 5, the month is written with a lowercase letter. It looks strange when compared to English :)

If you need to, you can change the order of the date.
Currently it's `L.dateFormat = "%s, %d %s %d г." -- Date format: "Monday 1 January 2025"`

But you can move this around, for example, `%2$d %1$s %3$s %4$d` would turn it into `1 Monday January 2025`

Here is an example from Chinese, where they want `dayname, y/m/d` `L.dateFormat = "%1$s，%4$d年%3$d%2$s日"`

payload.author: timurchak
payload.body:
> If you need to, you can change the order of the date. Currently it's `L.dateFormat = "%s, %d %s %d г." -- Date format: "Monday 1 January 2025"`
> 
> But you can move this around, for example, `%2$d %1$s %3$s %4$d` would turn it into `1 Monday January 2025`
> 
> Here is an example from Chinese, where they want `dayname, y/m/d` `L.dateFormat = "%1$s，%4$d年%3$d%2$s日"`

`L.dateFormat = "%s, %d %s %d г."` already looks correct for Russian.

`"Monday 5 August 2026"` -> `"Понедельник, 5 августа 2026 г."`


The month names are translated using the correct grammatical case for Russian dates (genitive case), so the generated date format reads naturally.
